User request: im about to paste our budget tab into a csv for the finance portal. that tab has a pile of SUMIFs in it and two references over to another sheet. what should i watch out for before i do that

content.text:
Short version: don’t export the live tab (with formulas and cross-sheet references) directly — CSVs only contain the visible values from one sheet and will drop formulas, other sheets, and formatting. Make a copy, resolve/flatten the formulas there, and verify formats/encoding before uploading.

Checklist (follow in order)
1. Make a backup copy of the workbook (preserve formulas). Never work on the original.
2. Know the CSV limitation: CSV saves only the active sheet’s visible values; formulas and other sheets are not preserved. If you save/export directly you will lose formulas and any cross-sheet links. (Microsoft: “When you save a workbook in CSV format, only the active sheet is saved… features not supported include multiple worksheets and formulas.”)  
   - Microsoft: https://support.microsoft.com/office/save-a-workbook-in-another-file-format-64d18e5b-9f50-4a99-9d42-2a8b6d3d7b01
3. Resolve the two cross-sheet references:
   - Either bring the referenced cells into the same sheet (copy their values) or
   - Replace the formulas that reference other sheets with their current values (Paste → Values) in the copy you’ll export.
   If you do nothing, the portal will only receive the current displayed values (not the formula), but you must ensure those values are correct and complete.
4. Flatten SUMIFs / formula-derived numbers:
   - If the portal expects static numbers, replace the SUMIF formulas with their calculated values in the export copy (copy → paste values). This prevents accidental recalculation differences after export.
   - Keep the original sheet with formulas for audit and future updates.
5. Check for formula errors and hidden items:
   - Scan for #REF!, #VALUE!, #NAME? or blank cells where formulas failed — fix before exporting.
   - Unhide rows/columns and clear any filtered-out rows if the portal needs them.
6. Verify totals and rounding:
   - SUMIFs can hide small floating-point differences. If the portal requires exact cents, round explicitly to the required precision (e.g., ROUND(...,2)) before flattening.
7. Formatting and data types:
   - Dates: convert to the portal’s required date format (ISO YYYY-MM-DD is safest).
   - Numbers: remove currency symbols and thousands separators if the portal expects plain numbers.
   - Leading zeros (IDs): ensure those fields are exported as text (prefix or format) so zeros aren’t dropped.
8. Delimiter, quoting, and encoding:
   - Confirm whether the portal wants comma-separated, semicolon, or another delimiter (locales sometimes use semicolons). CSV rules (quoting fields that contain commas/newlines) follow RFC 4180.  
     - RFC 4180: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4180
   - Export as UTF-8 to avoid character corruption (many portals expect UTF-8). Microsoft doc on CSV UTF-8: https://support.microsoft.com/office/save-a-csv-file-in-utf-8-format-0d3c9a98-d6a5-4e38-b6b7-27f3e4f5dfdf
9. Test a small export first:
   - Export a representative sample (or the whole file to a temp location) and open it in a plain-text editor to confirm delimiter, quoting, and encoding are correct, and numbers/dates look right.
10. Final verification before upload:
   - Reconcile key totals (grand total and a few random line items) between the original workbook and the CSV file you’ll upload.

If you tell me which system you use (Excel vs Google Sheets) and what the finance portal expects (delimiter, date/number formats, encoding), I can give step-by-step commands for a safe export and a quick verification routine.
